_doc: Mode-eval baseline fixtures. 19 categories, 53 total cases.
actual 8GB-Mac grocery dictation, with a `must_not_contain` grounding
check guarding against the leaked normal@v5 few-shot example.
Original 13 categories x 3 lengths = 39 cases (ADR 0024 Wave A/B/C).
Extension: 5 new categories added 2026-05-18 covering content types the
Each `raw` simulates Whisper STT output: mostly lowercase, light or no
punctuation, occasional disfluencies. `intent` describes speaker meaning.
`must_preserve` lists concepts that MUST appear in any cleaned output --
used for automated content-preservation scoring (case-insensitive substring).
in a group satisfies ALL terms in that group. Lets formal-mode paraphrases
`mode_hints` is per-mode optional notes for the human reviewer.
Authored by Bernard 2026-05-17, extended 2026-05-18 (ADR 0024 v2 corpus).

fixtures.raw: the question is whether to add a code mode and the answer is complicated because on one hand programmers dictate variable names and snippets all the time and a code mode would be valuable on the other hand the current three modes axis is register based and code is orthogonal to register so adding code would muddy the model and the third consideration is implementation cost which would mean a new prompt new few shot examples possibly a different model since code likely benefits from a coder model so probably we should not add it yet but revisit after the empirical tuning is done and we have a clearer sense of where the modes are weakest
fixtures.intent: Detailed Q&A about whether to add a code mode, weighing three considerations.

fixtures.raw: the architecture is that the dictation thread owns an arc mutex connection and shares a clone with the orchestrator which in turn shares another clone with the cleaner so when cleanup runs it can issue its own queries for the prompt the dictionary and the few shot examples without negotiating borrows across the orchestrators persist transaction and this works because rusqlite connections are themselves single threaded but the mutex serializes access across the threads that hold clones
fixtures.intent: Architecture explanation: shared DB connection via Arc<Mutex<Connection>>.

mode_hints.formal: could become 'Architecture overview' with structured explanation

fixtures.raw: okay let me lay out the full architecture for mockingbird v2 the foundation layer covers the audio capture which uses cpal and the voice activity detection which uses silero through the ort runtime and the speech to text which uses whisper rs with cuda the processing layer covers the deterministic preprocessor which strips fillers and stutters and renders verbal cues and the llm cleanup which uses ollama with three modes casual normal and formal the storage layer covers the sqlite database with rusqlite for the raw transcripts and the cleaned outputs and the prompt versions and finally the surface layer covers the tauri windows the system tray the global hotkey through the windows low level keyboard hook and the injection pipeline which does clipboard save restore around every paste
fixtures.intent: Full architecture description with four named layers each containing 3-5 components, naming specific libraries and concepts.

fixtures.raw: alright the algorithm works like this you start by reading the raw whisper output then you pass it through the preprocessor which is a chain of regex passes that handle fillers like um and uh then stutter collapse like i i i became i then verbal cues like new line and bullet then quote handling and the output of the preprocessor goes into the llm via ollama with the resolved prompt body and the per mode temperature and the result gets stored in the cleaned column of the transcripts table along with the prompt id and the preprocessor version and the cleanup ms timing field for telemetry then finally we kick off the injection pipeline which saves the clipboard pastes our text and restores the clipboard after a short delay
fixtures.intent: End-to-end algorithm description spanning preprocessor, LLM call, DB columns, and injection.
